Ask Sam about glass

Ways glass is fixed

The fixing decides how the glass looks and how strong it is. Ask Sam which suits your project.

Framed

Glass held in an aluminium or timber frame. Best for windows and sliding doors.

Frameless

Clean edges with minimal hardware. Popular for showers and partitions.

Channel fixed

Glass set into a floor or base channel. Common for balustrades and shopfronts.

Point fixed

Glass held by metal fittings at the corners, for canopies and large facades.

Pivot and hinged doors

Glass doors on floor or wall hinges, for entrances and offices.

Structural glazing

Large panels bonded to a building frame. Used on tall buildings.

Our glass range

Sam can supply and fit the main glass types used in homes, shops and offices. Ask for samples on site.

Clear glass

Bright and see-through, for windows, doors and shopfronts.

Frosted glass

Soft, private light for bathrooms and meeting rooms.

Reeded glass

Vertical ribs that blur what is behind while keeping the light.

Tinted glass

Bronze and grey tints that cut glare and heat.

Ombre glass

A tint that fades from dark to clear, popular for partitions.

Tempered glass

Toughened for strength. Used for showers, doors and partitions.

Laminated glass

Two layers bonded together, so it holds if it cracks. Used for balustrades.

How a glass job runs

  1. Measure

    Sam measures the opening and checks it is square and level.

  2. Choose

    You pick the glass type, finish and fittings.

  3. Cut and toughen

    Glass is cut to size before toughening, because it can’t be cut afterwards.

  4. Fit and seal

    Installed, sealed and cleaned, then checked with you.

More than a finished surface

Each project starts with a look at the space and a conversation about the finish. The clips above show different kinds of work; these notes explain what to consider before work begins. Every property is different, so Sam confirms measurements, materials, scope and quote during the site visit.

Painting and preparation

Walls are checked and prepared before paint goes on. Filling, skimming, sealing and choosing a finish suited to the surface all help create an even result. Sam handles interior and exterior painting, including textured and spray finishes.

Ceilings and lighting

Gypsum and POP ceilings can be plain, stepped or curved, with cove and LED lighting details. Discuss ceiling height, lighting positions and edges early, so the finished layout works with the room and its existing fittings.

Feature walls

A feature wall can combine an accent colour or texture with TV and display niches. Decide what the wall needs to hold, where lighting will sit, and how the finish connects with nearby surfaces before work begins.

Exterior surfaces

Exterior walls, gates and fences need a finish suited to their exposure and use. Preparation comes before the weather-ready coat. Sam checks the surface and scope on site, then confirms the work in the written quote.

Windows and glass

For windows, doors, shower screens and partitions, the frame and opening are checked before the glass is confirmed. Clear, tinted and frosted options suit different needs for light and privacy. Measurements and fixing details are agreed before fitting.

Balustrades and details

Balustrade work is planned around the opening, supports and intended use. Glass type, fittings and site conditions affect the specification, so Sam confirms measurements and suitable fixing details in person before preparing a quote.

From the first visit to handover

A clear process keeps the work aligned with what you asked for. The exact schedule depends on the project and is confirmed with your quote.

  1. Site visit

    Talk through the job. Sam checks the surfaces or openings, takes measurements and notes the details that affect the work.

  2. Scope and quote

    Agree the finish, materials and work required. Sam provides a written quote so the scope and price are clear before starting.

  3. Preparation and fitting

    The surfaces or frames are prepared, then the agreed painting, ceiling, feature-wall or glass work is completed with the site kept tidy.

  4. Review and handover

    Walk through the finished work together, check the agreed details and raise anything that needs attention before handover.
